item.content:encoded:
The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) and the NIHR Maternity Disparities Consortium (MDC) are offering exciting opportunities for researchers and aspiring doctoral scholars interested in data science, statistics, epidemiology, public health, health inequalities and maternity research.

These opportunities provide applicants with the chance to contribute to major research programmes focused on improving health outcomes, addressing inequalities and using large-scale routinely collected healthcare data to generate evidence that can influence policy and practice.

There are two closely related opportunities to consider. The first is for Research Fellows in Data Science, Statistics or Epidemiology at LSHTM, while the second is a funded PhD studentship under the NIHR Inequalities Challenge: Maternity Disparities Consortium.

Both opportunities are particularly relevant to candidates with strong quantitative research skills who are interested in using advanced analytical methods and large datasets to tackle important public health challenges.

1. LSHTM Research Fellow in Data Science, Statistics or Epidemiology

The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine is recruiting two Research Fellows to join the Department of Health Services Research & Policy.

The successful researchers will work within the DELTA core function of the NIHR Maternity Disparities Consortium, a major national programme designed to improve maternity and neonatal outcomes across the United Kingdom and reduce inequalities before, during and after pregnancy.

The position presents an excellent opportunity for researchers who want to develop or advance a career in big data research, healthcare analytics, epidemiology, statistics or health services research.

About the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine

LSHTM is internationally recognised for its work in public health, tropical medicine, epidemiology, health policy and global health research.

Its mission is to improve health and health equity in the UK and worldwide through research, education, partnerships and the translation of evidence into policy and practice.

Researchers joining LSHTM can therefore expect to work in an academically strong environment where research findings can contribute to real-world health and policy decisions.

2. What the Research Fellow Role Involves

The Research Fellows will be involved in analysing routinely collected linked national datasets covering mothers and babies in England.

This means the researchers will have the opportunity to work with large-scale healthcare data and conduct sophisticated analyses to better understand maternity outcomes and disparities.

The role is particularly suited to someone who wants to develop expertise in:

  • Data science
  • Statistics
  • Epidemiology
  • Healthcare data analysis
  • Health services research
  • Large observational studies
  • Routinely collected healthcare data
  • Linked national datasets
  • Quantitative research
  • Public health research
  • Maternity and neonatal outcomes
  • Health inequalities

The successful candidate may come from a background in large observational healthcare studies, although experience analysing clinical trials may also be relevant.

The position is therefore not restricted exclusively to applicants whose previous research has focused on maternity care. Candidates with strong methodological and quantitative research experience may also be suitable.

3. Research Fellow Positions and Working Arrangement

There are two positions available.

The posts are:

  • Based in the Department of Health Services Research & Policy
  • Located in London
  • Available full-time or part-time
  • Between 17.5 and 35 hours per week
  • Equivalent to 0.5–1.0 FTE
  • Fixed-term until 31 May 2028

One position is available immediately, while the second position is scheduled to become available from 1 September 2026.

This flexibility may make the opportunity particularly attractive to researchers who are looking for either a full-time research career or a part-time research appointment.

4. Research Fellow Salary and Benefits

The salary is on the LSHTM Grade 6 salary scale:

£45,728 to £51,872 per annum pro rata, inclusive of London Weighting.

Because the positions can be part-time, the salary is paid on a pro-rata basis depending on the individual’s FTE appointment.

Additional benefits include:

  • 30 working days of annual leave per year, pro rata for part-time staff
  • Discretionary Wellbeing Days
  • Access to the Pension Scheme
  • Employment under LSHTM terms and conditions of service
  • The opportunity to work within a leading public health research institution
  • Experience working with large-scale linked national healthcare datasets
  • Exposure to major national research programmes

The role could therefore provide valuable experience for researchers seeking to build a long-term career in academic research, health data science, epidemiology, statistics or public health.

5. Who Should Consider the Research Fellow Position?

The role is particularly appropriate for applicants with strong expertise in data science, statistics or epidemiology.

The successful applicant is expected to have a postgraduate qualification, with a doctoral degree ideally preferred, in a relevant field.

Candidates with experience in analysing large observational healthcare datasets would be especially relevant, although applicants with experience analysing clinical trial data may also be considered.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate strong quantitative and analytical capabilities and an interest in using research evidence to understand healthcare outcomes and inequalities.

6. NIHR Maternity Disparities Consortium PhD Studentship

The second opportunity is part of the NIHR Inequalities Challenge: Maternity Disparities Consortium.

The Consortium is offering up to 13 funded PhD studentships across a range of projects hosted by universities within the Consortium.

The programme is designed to develop the next generation of researchers capable of addressing persistent inequalities in maternity and neonatal health.

The studentships are particularly focused on strengthening research capacity in methodological areas where additional expertise is needed.

These areas include, but are not limited to:

  • Health economics
  • Statistics
  • Trial design
  • Digital research
  • Data science
  • Implementation science
  • Co-production methods
  • Quantitative research
  • Health inequalities research

The PhD programme is therefore broader than maternity clinical research alone. Applicants with methodological expertise who can apply their skills to maternity inequalities are encouraged to consider the opportunity.

7. About the Maternity Disparities Consortium

The NIHR Maternity Disparities Consortium is a UK-wide collaboration involving:

  • Universities
  • NHS trusts
  • Local councils
  • Charities
  • Industry partners
  • Researchers
  • Communities
  • Other organisations working to improve maternity outcomes

The Consortium aims to improve outcomes for women and babies before, during and after pregnancy while developing a new generation of research leaders.

Its capacity development programme focuses on building long-term research expertise and strengthening the workforce required to deliver sustainable improvements in maternity health.

Particular emphasis is placed on research capacity in underrepresented disciplines, professions and underserved communities.

8. The Featured PhD Research Project

One of the available projects is titled:

“Developing a unified conceptual and measurement framework of maternity inequalities to inform policy using routinely collected national data.”

The project is based at LSHTM and is identified by the project code:

D1.2_LSHTM

The research will investigate how different forms of disadvantage contribute to inequalities in maternity outcomes.

The project recognises that maternity inequalities can be influenced by multiple interacting factors rather than by a single characteristic.

While existing UK research has extensively examined factors such as ethnicity and area-based deprivation, there is comparatively less research examining other determinants and how multiple disadvantages interact.

The project therefore aims to develop better ways of identifying and measuring these factors using routinely collected national data.

9. Why This Research Matters

Understanding maternity inequalities requires more than identifying which groups experience poorer outcomes.

Researchers also need to understand:

  • What causes these inequalities
  • Which factors contribute to disadvantage
  • How different disadvantages interact
  • Which populations experience multiple forms of disadvantage
  • How inequalities influence access to maternity services
  • How inequalities affect health outcomes
  • Which interventions could reduce these inequalities
  • Which policies are most likely to benefit populations experiencing the greatest disadvantage

At present, routinely collected national datasets do not always contain standardised or reliable measurements for all relevant determinants of disadvantage.

The proposed PhD will therefore attempt to improve how these factors are measured and analysed.

This could help researchers and policymakers identify vulnerable populations more accurately and design interventions that are better targeted to their circumstances.

10. Main Aim of the PhD Project

The overall aim is to develop a conceptual and measurement framework for maternity inequalities.

The framework will seek to provide a better understanding of:

  • Individual-level determinants of disadvantage
  • Household-level determinants
  • Place-based determinants
  • Relationships between different determinants
  • Mechanisms through which disadvantage affects maternity outcomes
  • The accumulation of multiple disadvantages
  • Interactions between different forms of disadvantage

The research will combine theoretical approaches with data-driven methods and applied studies using routinely collected national datasets.

11. Research Objectives

The PhD project has three major research objectives.

Objective 1: Conduct a realist review and framework synthesis

The first stage will involve a comprehensive review of existing evidence.

The researcher will conduct a realist review and framework synthesis to identify determinants of inequality and develop an understanding of the plausible pathways through which these factors influence maternity outcomes.

This will help establish the theoretical foundation for the project.

Objective 2: Develop standardised measurement and coding frameworks

The second objective involves developing standardised and validated coding frameworks that can be used to measure determinants of disadvantage in routinely collected national datasets.

The project will use data science methods to improve the identification and measurement of factors that may currently be poorly captured.

Particular attention will be given to under-researched factors including:

  • Disability
  • Neurodivergent conditions
  • Language needs
  • Interpreter requirements
  • Migration status
  • Mental health conditions
  • Gender-based violence
  • Food insecurity
  • Housing insecurity

This component could involve significant data management, coding, statistical analysis and methodological development.

Objective 3: Apply the frameworks to maternity research

The third objective will involve applying the newly developed frameworks in up to three studies.

These studies may examine:

  • How different determinants accumulate
  • How multiple forms of disadvantage interact
  • The relationship between disadvantage and maternity outcomes
  • Family outcomes
  • The potential effects of interventions on different populations
  • How advanced statistical methods can be used to model intervention effects

This stage will allow the researcher to demonstrate how the framework works in practical research settings.

12. Expected Impact of the PhD

The project is expected to contribute to maternity health equity research by combining theory-driven and data-driven approaches.

The research could help demonstrate both the strengths and limitations of routinely collected healthcare data when conducting equity-focused research.

A major intended outcome is to improve the identification of populations experiencing multiple or intersecting forms of disadvantage.

Better measurement could ultimately help researchers and policymakers:

  1. Identify populations at increased risk more accurately.
  2. Understand the mechanisms behind maternity inequalities.
  3. Design more targeted interventions.
  4. Evaluate policies aimed at reducing inequalities.
  5. Improve the evidence available to national studies.
  6. Support the development and scaling of effective interventions.
  7. Strengthen maternity health policy.
  8. Apply the resulting methodological approaches beyond maternity care.
  9. Potentially adapt the methods for use in other countries and healthcare systems.

The project’s impact therefore extends beyond the immediate maternity research setting.

13. Funding Package for the PhD Studentship

The PhD studentships provide substantial financial support.

Successful students will receive:

Full tuition fees

Full home tuition fees will be covered at the applicable 2026/27 UK rates.

Annual tax-free stipend

The studentship provides a tax-free annual stipend at UKRI rates.

The stated rates are:

  • £21,805 outside London
  • £23,805 inside London

The London rate applies from 1 October 2026 as stated in the opportunity information.

Research and training allowance

Each award also includes a:

£5,000 contribution towards research, travel, training and consumables.

This can provide valuable additional support for activities required during the doctoral research.

14. Duration and Start Date

The PhD programme is scheduled to begin in:

January 2027

The duration can be:

  • Up to 3 years full-time, or
  • Up to 4 years at 0.8 WTE part-time, where this arrangement can be agreed.

Students will be required to meet the regulations and registration requirements of their host university.

15. International Students Can Apply

International applicants are welcome to apply for the PhD studentships.

However, there is an important financial condition for international candidates.

The studentship covers full home tuition fees at the relevant UK rate, but international applicants must secure alternative funding to cover the difference between UK and overseas tuition fees.

International candidates must also be prepared to provide proof of funding for international fees and immigration costs before their interview if they are shortlisted.

This is an important consideration for applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, Latin America, the Caribbean, Oceania and other regions outside the UK.

Applicants should therefore carefully assess the total cost of overseas tuition and immigration requirements before submitting an application.

16. Eligibility Requirements for the PhD

Applicants should meet the essential eligibility criteria.

Academic qualification

Applicants must normally hold:

  • A First-Class or Upper Second-Class Honours degree, equivalent to a UK 2:1 or above, in a relevant subject.

Relevant disciplines may include:

  • Statistics
  • Applied Mathematics
  • Data Science
  • Computer Science
  • Or a similar quantitative or methodological discipline

An overseas qualification equivalent to the required UK academic standard is acceptable.

Master’s degree

A Master’s degree or equivalent in a relevant field is recommended.

While the information describes the Master’s as recommended rather than an absolute essential requirement, applicants should assess their academic profile against the specific requirements of the host institution.

Research experience

Applicants should have relevant previous research experience.

This experience may relate to either:

  • The substantive research area, or
  • The methodological area.

Therefore, applicants do not necessarily need to have previously specialised in maternity research if they can demonstrate strong methodological expertise and explain how their background can contribute to research on maternity inequalities.

Quantitative research skills

Applicants should have strong quantitative research skills and experience analysing complex datasets.

Experience with routinely collected data would be particularly advantageous.

Commitment to maternity inequalities

Applicants should demonstrate an understanding of and commitment to tackling maternity inequalities.

This is particularly important because the project is designed to address disparities in health outcomes and access to care.

Communication

Applicants should demonstrate excellent:

  • Written communication skills
  • Verbal communication skills
  • Academic communication
  • Research communication

Independence and teamwork

Candidates should be:

  • Highly motivated
  • Able to work independently
  • Able to work effectively as part of a team
  • Capable of planning and managing their own workload

17. Who Is Particularly Encouraged to Apply?

The NIHR Maternity Disparities Consortium states that it particularly encourages applications from people who are passionate about maternity health equity and who can contribute relevant methodological knowledge and experience.

The programme specifically encourages applications from:

  • People from underrepresented ethnic backgrounds
  • People with disabilities
  • Neurodivergent people
  • People with long-term health requirements
  • Candidates of all genders
  • Candidates of all ages
  • Candidates of all beliefs
  • Applicants with experience in a broad range of research methodologies

Applicants should not assume that they are unsuitable simply because their previous academic discipline is not explicitly labelled “maternity research.”

If the connection between their academic background and maternity inequalities is not immediately obvious, applicants are encouraged to clearly explain that connection in their cover letter.

18. Application Process for the PhD Studentship

The PhD application process takes place in several stages.

Stage One: Initial Application

Applicants must submit their application by:

5:00 PM, Monday 7 September 2026

Candidates may apply for a maximum of two projects.

If applying for more than one project, applicants may either submit:

  • One covering letter addressing both projects, or
  • A separate covering letter for each project.

Applicants are required to submit:

  • A two-page CV
  • At least one covering letter
  • Details of two referees
  • At least one academic referee

The application documents must follow the specified naming convention:

Surname_CV_project code

and

Surname_CL_project code

Applicants should pay close attention to these instructions because failure to provide the required documents or information could affect the application.

APPLY HERE

19. Stage Two: Interview and LSHTM Registration Application

Candidates who are shortlisted will progress to the interview stage.

Shortlisted candidates will also be required to complete the LSHTM RD application process by 1 October 2026.

The national panel interviews are scheduled for:

Thursday 15 and Friday 16 October 2026

The interviews will take place in Newcastle.

Candidates who apply for two projects and are selected to interview for both will, where possible, be scheduled so that they only need to attend one interview.

Applicants should nevertheless make appropriate arrangements to attend the interview dates if shortlisted.

20. Stage Three: University Placement

Successful candidates will be required to register for a PhD at the relevant host institution.

Being selected through the Consortium does not remove the requirement to satisfy the individual university’s postgraduate admission requirements.

Applicants should therefore check the relevant university’s:

  • PhD entry requirements
  • Registration requirements
  • English language requirements
  • Immigration requirements where applicable
  • Funding conditions
  • Other postgraduate admissions criteria

Candidates should also contact the lead supervisor if they need clarification about the project or their suitability.

21. English Language Requirement

Applicants must satisfy the stated LSHTM Band B English language requirement.

Candidates should check the applicable LSHTM requirements carefully, particularly if their previous education was conducted outside an accepted English-language framework.

22. Important Dates

Applicants should take note of the following dates.

PhD Studentship

Application deadline: 5:00 PM, Monday 7 September 2026

LSHTM RD application deadline for shortlisted candidates: 1 October 2026

Interview dates: Thursday 15 and Friday 16 October 2026

Expected PhD start date: January 2027

Research Fellow Position

Application deadline: Thursday 27 August 2026

The LSHTM automated application system will accept online applications until 10:00 PM on the closing date.

The Research Fellow position carries the reference:

PHP-HSRP-2026-15

Applicants should quote this reference when making enquiries about the position.

23. How to Apply for the Research Fellow Position

Applications for the Research Fellow position should be submitted online through the LSHTM jobs website Here

The supporting statement is an especially important part of the application.

Applicants must use the supporting statement to demonstrate how their:

  • Qualifications
  • Professional experience
  • Research experience
  • Training
  • Technical skills
  • Methodological knowledge

meet each of the selection criteria.

Applicants should provide one or more paragraphs addressing each criterion.

Simply writing “Please see attached CV” is not considered an acceptable response.

Because the supporting statement is an essential part of the selection process, applicants should treat it as a central component of the application rather than as an administrative formality.

24. How to Strengthen Your Application

Applicants can improve their chances by making their application highly specific to the opportunity.

For the Research Fellow position

Your application should clearly demonstrate:

  • Your postgraduate or doctoral qualification
  • Expertise in data science, statistics or epidemiology
  • Experience with quantitative research
  • Experience analysing large datasets
  • Experience with healthcare or routinely collected data where applicable
  • Experience with observational studies or clinical trials
  • Statistical and analytical software skills
  • Understanding of health services research
  • Interest in maternity inequalities
  • Ability to work independently
  • Ability to collaborate with multidisciplinary teams

Avoid submitting a generic research CV or generic supporting statement.

Instead, explicitly connect your previous research to the DELTA function and the NIHR Maternity Disparities Consortium.

For the PhD studentship

Your two-page CV should prioritise:

  • Relevant academic qualifications
  • Quantitative research experience
  • Research projects
  • Data analysis experience
  • Statistical methods
  • Relevant publications or research outputs
  • Dissertation or thesis experience
  • Research software and technical skills
  • Relevant professional or academic experience

Your cover letter should clearly explain:

  1. Why you are interested in maternity inequalities.
  2. Why this particular project interests you.
  3. What methodological skills you bring.
  4. How your previous research prepares you for the project.
  5. Why routinely collected national data is an important area of research.
  6. How your background could contribute to the project’s objectives.
  7. Why you are prepared for doctoral-level research.

25. Research Areas That Could Make an Applicant Stand Out

Applicants with experience in areas such as the following may find their skills particularly relevant:

  • Epidemiological analysis
  • Biostatistics
  • Data science
  • Machine learning
  • Health economics
  • Statistical modelling
  • Causal inference
  • Clinical research
  • Health services research
  • Administrative healthcare datasets
  • Electronic health records
  • Linked datasets
  • Data management
  • Quantitative social research
  • Implementation science
  • Digital health
  • Public health
  • Health inequalities research

However, applicants should not assume that possessing one specific technical skill guarantees eligibility.

The Consortium explicitly welcomes applicants with a range of methodological backgrounds, provided they can demonstrate how their expertise can contribute to research on maternity inequalities.

26. Why Routinely Collected Data Is Central to These Opportunities

One of the most important themes running through both opportunities is the use of routinely collected healthcare data.

Routine data can provide researchers with information about very large populations and can allow researchers to examine health outcomes across different demographic, geographic and social groups.

However, such datasets can also have limitations.

Some important characteristics may be incompletely recorded, inconsistently coded or difficult to identify.

This is particularly important when studying health inequalities.

For example, researchers may need better ways of identifying:

  • Disability
  • Neurodivergence
  • Language barriers
  • Migration status
  • Mental health conditions
  • Experiences of gender-based violence
  • Food insecurity
  • Housing insecurity

The proposed PhD therefore addresses an important methodological challenge: improving the ability of researchers to measure complex and intersecting forms of disadvantage using existing national data.

27. A Major Opportunity for International Researchers

The PhD programme is particularly noteworthy for international applicants because the Consortium explicitly states that international students are welcome to apply.

However, international applicants should understand the financial arrangement before applying.

The studentship provides funding at the home-fee level, meaning international applicants must identify additional funding to cover the difference between UK and overseas tuition fees.

They may also need funding for immigration-related expenses.

International candidates who are shortlisted must be able to provide evidence of the necessary additional funding before their interview.

This makes early financial planning essential for applicants outside the UK.

28. Location and Research Environment

The Research Fellow positions are based at LSHTM in London.

The PhD studentship is part of a wider UK Consortium, meaning the host university and location will depend on the selected project.

For the featured D1.2_LSHTM project, LSHTM is the relevant institution and Ipek Gurol-Urganci is identified as the contact supervisor.

The wider Consortium brings together institutions and organisations across the UK, creating opportunities for collaboration between academia, healthcare services, government-related organisations, communities and other partners.

29. Contact Information

For questions relating specifically to the LSHTM Research Fellow position, applicants can contact:

Ipek Gurol Urganci
ipek.gurol@lshtm.ac.uk

Jan van der Meulen
jan.vandermeulen@lshtm.ac.uk

For application-process questions concerning the Research Fellow position:

jobs@lshtm.ac.uk

Applicants should quote:

PHP-HSRP-2026-15

For more information about LSHTM Research Fellow position, visit HERE

For general enquiries concerning the NIHR Maternity Disparities Consortium capacity development programme or reasonable adjustments for the application or interview process:

nihr.mdc.capacitydevelopment@newcastle.ac.uk

For questions about the featured PhD project:

Ipek Gurol-Urganci
ipek.gurol@lshtm.ac.uk

Applicants are encouraged to contact individual supervisors if they want to discuss the research project or their suitability before applying.

Click HERE to view more information about the NIHR Maternity Disparities Consortium capacity development programme

30. Accessibility and Support

The Consortium states that it wants applicants to perform at their best and recognises that some candidates may require reasonable adjustments during the application or interview process.

Examples may include:

  • Alternative formats
  • Additional time
  • Specific technological arrangements
  • Other reasonable adjustments

Applicants who require support should contact the Consortium’s capacity development team as early as possible.

The programme also has an equality-monitoring process. Applicants may receive an Equality Monitoring Form during the application period.

The information collected through this process is intended to monitor equal opportunities and is handled separately from the application.

31. Which Opportunity Is Right for You?

The two opportunities are aimed at different stages of an individual’s research career.

Consider the Research Fellow position if you:

  • Already hold a relevant postgraduate qualification.
  • Have substantial quantitative research experience.
  • Have experience analysing complex datasets.
  • Have expertise in statistics, epidemiology or data science.
  • Want to work professionally as a researcher.
  • Are interested in large-scale healthcare data.
  • Want to contribute to national maternity research.
  • Are interested in a fixed-term research appointment through May 2028.

Consider the PhD studentship if you:

  • Are seeking doctoral-level research training.
  • Have a relevant Bachelor’s degree at 2:1 or above or an equivalent overseas qualification.
  • Have relevant research experience.
  • Have strong quantitative research skills.
  • Are interested in data science, statistics, epidemiology or related methodologies.
  • Want to research maternity inequalities.
  • Are prepared to undertake up to three years of full-time doctoral research.
  • Can satisfy the host university’s PhD requirements.
  • If international, can secure the additional funding required for overseas tuition and immigration costs.

32. Key Takeaways

These opportunities provide several important pathways into public health and health inequalities research.

The Research Fellow positions offer the opportunity to work directly with large-scale linked national datasets involving mothers and babies in England while developing expertise in data science, statistics, epidemiology and health services research.

The PhD studentships provide an opportunity to undertake advanced methodological research while contributing to the broader objective of reducing maternity inequalities.

The featured PhD project is particularly significant because it seeks to improve the measurement of multiple and intersecting forms of disadvantage using routinely collected national data.

For aspiring researchers, the combination of methodological training, large-scale data analysis and real-world health policy relevance makes these opportunities particularly valuable.

Visit the OFY Website HERE for more fellowship and job opportunities

Conclusion

The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine and the NIHR Maternity Disparities Consortium are providing significant opportunities for researchers interested in using data, statistics and epidemiological methods to address major public health challenges.

The Research Fellow positions offer an opportunity for experienced researchers to contribute to a major national programme examining maternity and neonatal outcomes across England, with a particular emphasis on analysing linked national datasets and understanding health inequalities.

Meanwhile, the NIHR Maternity Disparities Consortium PhD programme offers up to 13 funded doctoral opportunities beginning in January 2027. The featured LSHTM project will investigate how individual, household and place-based factors contribute to maternity inequalities and will use advanced data science and statistical approaches to improve the measurement of disadvantage.

Applicants should pay particular attention to the different deadlines. The Research Fellow application closes on Thursday 27 August 2026 at 10:00 PM, while the PhD studentship application closes at 5:00 PM on Monday 7 September 2026.

Candidates should also ensure that their supporting statements and cover letters directly address the relevant selection criteria rather than relying on their CV alone.

For international PhD applicants, the opportunity is open to applications from outside the UK, but additional funding will be required to cover the difference between UK and overseas tuition fees as well as applicable immigration costs.

Overall, these opportunities are well suited to academically and quantitatively strong candidates who want to build careers in public health research, epidemiology, statistics, data science, health services research and health equity. They also provide an opportunity to contribute to research with the potential to influence policy, improve healthcare and address inequalities affecting women, babies and families.

item.content:encoded:
The University of Pennsylvania (UPenn), through its Institute for the Advanced Study of India (UPIASI), in collaboration with Microsoft Research India, is inviting applications for two Research Fellow positions for recent graduates who intend to pursue a Ph.D. The fellows will work on research and development projects focused on using artificial intelligence to improve outcomes in health, education, communication, and media in India.

The two positions are designed to bring together academic research, artificial intelligence, field experimentation, technology development, and real-world deployment. Successful candidates will become full members of the research team, contributing to the development of AI systems, field studies, evaluations, data analysis, research papers, and other research outputs.

The positions are particularly suited to graduates interested in AI research, development economics, public policy, education technology, public health, computer science, data science, human-computer interaction, natural language processing, applied statistics, and technology for social impact.

Both positions are appointed through the University of Pennsylvania Institute for the Advanced Study of India and hosted at Microsoft Research in Bengaluru, India, with regular travel to field sites in Rajasthan, Delhi, and other locations in India.

Overview of the UPenn and Microsoft Research Fellowship

The new research program at the University of Pennsylvania’s Center for the Advanced Study of India is built around a field-first approach to artificial intelligence research.

Rather than developing AI systems exclusively in controlled laboratory environments, the research team aims to understand how these technologies work when they are introduced into real communities, institutions, classrooms, healthcare environments, and media ecosystems.

The program emphasizes three important stages:

  1. Co-designing AI tools with local partners
  2. Deploying the tools under real-world conditions
  3. Evaluating the tools against the alternatives that people currently use

This approach is intended to produce AI systems that are not only technically effective but also culturally appropriate, practical, sustainable, and useful in the environments where they are deployed.

The fellows will therefore have an opportunity to work at the intersection of academic research and practical AI deployment.

Two Research Fellow Positions Are Available

The recruitment is for two complementary pre-doctoral Research Fellow positions.

1. Research Fellow – Field Research and Evaluation

The first position focuses primarily on the research, fieldwork, study design, evaluation, and data analysis side of the program.

The successful fellow will be responsible for helping design and manage studies that evaluate AI systems in real-world environments.

Key responsibilities and areas of work include:

  • Designing research studies
  • Developing evaluation strategies
  • Supporting Institutional Review Board (IRB) processes and partner approvals
  • Coordinating field teams
  • Working with survey firms and research partners
  • Managing data collection
  • Monitoring data quality
  • Conducting statistical analysis
  • Contributing to research papers
  • Evaluating AI tools against existing alternatives and practices
  • Supporting research implementation in field locations
  • Helping determine whether AI interventions produce meaningful improvements

This position would be particularly relevant to graduates with backgrounds in economics, public policy, development studies, statistics, or related disciplines.

Candidates with hands-on experience managing randomized controlled trials or comparable field studies are especially relevant to this role.

Experience at organizations or research institutions such as J-PAL, IPA, or equivalent research-management environments would be considered valuable.

2. Research Fellow – Tool Development and Deployment

The second position focuses on the development, implementation, deployment, and evaluation of AI-powered tools.

This role is intended for candidates with strong technical backgrounds who are interested in understanding how technology performs outside controlled laboratory environments.

The successful candidate may work on areas including:

  • Artificial intelligence
  • Machine learning
  • Natural language processing
  • Human-computer interaction
  • Data science
  • Applied statistics
  • Software and tool development
  • AI deployment
  • Data analysis
  • Technology for public health
  • Education technology
  • AI applications in media

The role also requires an interest in fieldwork because the systems being developed will ultimately be tested and used in real-world environments.

Candidates with a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related field are particularly encouraged to consider this position.

Research Areas Covered by the Fellowship

The fellows will contribute to several major research programs. These projects address practical problems in health, education, communication, and media.

Samvaad: AI Practice for Frontline Health Workers

One of the research programs is called Samvaad, which focuses on using AI to support India’s frontline health workers.

India has approximately one million Accredited Social Health Activists, commonly known as ASHAs. These workers perform important health-related and community-facing responsibilities.

Their work includes counseling families on issues such as:

  • Contraception
  • Vaccination
  • Antenatal care
  • Family health
  • Other health-related decisions

However, health communication can be challenging because health workers sometimes have to address resistance or disagreement arising from household power dynamics and other social factors.

The research team is working with Khushi Baby to develop voice-based role-play tools that can help ASHAs practice difficult conversations.

The objective is to explore whether AI-powered practice environments can strengthen communication skills and improve the effectiveness of frontline health workers.

A fellow working on this program could therefore be involved in AI development, field deployment, research design, behavioral evaluation, data analysis, or a combination of these activities.

Clinical Communication Training with AIIMS New Delhi

Another research stream focuses on clinical communication training in partnership with AIIMS New Delhi.

Healthcare professionals frequently have to communicate difficult information to patients and caregivers. These conversations can involve complex medical, emotional, and interpersonal challenges.

The research team is developing and evaluating an AI-based communication training tool intended to help clinicians improve their communication and counseling abilities.

This work builds on previous research published at CSCW 2025.

For researchers interested in healthcare technology, human-computer interaction, AI-assisted training, public health, or communication, this research stream provides an opportunity to investigate how AI can support professional development in healthcare settings.

Bolo: AI Speaking Partners for Low-Income Classrooms

The Bolo research program focuses on spoken English and educational opportunity.

Spoken English can play an important role in economic mobility in India. However, students who could potentially benefit most from additional language practice often have fewer opportunities to practice speaking.

The research team previously field-tested an early version of a voice-based practice chatbot across four low-fee schools in Delhi.

That work was published at CHI 2026.

The next stage of the project will involve delivering a mobile-first version of the tool for sustained classroom use.

Researchers will evaluate outcomes including:

  • English fluency
  • Student confidence
  • Willingness to communicate
  • Opportunities for speaking practice
  • How students interact with AI-based speaking partners
  • The effectiveness of AI-supported language learning compared with existing approaches

This research stream could be particularly interesting to applicants interested in education technology, AI, natural language processing, HCI, learning sciences, or social-impact technology.

Kahani: AI, Entertainment Media and Social Norms

The Kahani research stream explores how entertainment media can influence social norms.

The project builds on an analysis of more than 250,000 films and television series across more than 20 countries.

The research examines how gender norms and other prosocial themes are communicated through:

  • Films
  • Television
  • Digital media
  • Entertainment content
  • Other forms of popular media

The program also seeks to develop tools that can help:

  • Researchers
  • Policymakers
  • Creative industries
  • Other stakeholders

better understand and strengthen the positive social impact of entertainment media.

Applicants interested in AI, computational social science, media studies, gender and social norms research, data analysis, public policy, or digital media may find this research stream particularly relevant.

A Field-First Approach to Artificial Intelligence Research

A major distinguishing feature of these positions is the emphasis on taking AI beyond the laboratory.

The research team is interested in questions such as:

  • Does an AI tool actually work when deployed in real communities?
  • How do users interact with AI systems under real-world conditions?
  • How does an AI intervention compare with existing alternatives?
  • Are AI tools culturally appropriate?
  • Can communities and institutions realistically sustain these technologies?
  • What happens when technology is introduced into schools, healthcare environments, or media ecosystems?
  • Can AI interventions produce measurable improvements in people’s lives?

The research program therefore combines technology development with rigorous evaluation.

This means fellows may not simply be building AI systems or conducting statistical analysis in isolation. They may be involved in understanding the entire lifecycle of an intervention, from design and development to deployment and evaluation.

Previous Research and Academic Work

The research program builds on previous work published at major academic venues.

The call references work associated with:

  • CHI 2026
  • CSCW 2025
  • IC2S2 2026
  • NAACL 2025

This provides prospective fellows with the opportunity to work within an active research environment connected to established academic research in AI, human-computer interaction, computational social science, communication, and related disciplines.

Who Is the Research Fellow Position Designed For?

The Research Fellow positions are intended primarily for recent graduates who plan to pursue a Ph.D.

The program follows the general model of the Microsoft Research India Research Fellow program, where fellows gain substantial research experience before potentially progressing to doctoral study.

Fellows will work as full members of the research team rather than simply performing administrative or support functions.

Their work may include:

  • Building AI systems
  • Designing research studies
  • Running field experiments
  • Deploying technology
  • Collecting data
  • Analyzing datasets
  • Evaluating interventions
  • Contributing to academic papers
  • Working with research partners
  • Participating in field activities
  • Supporting real-world technology implementation

For graduates considering a future Ph.D., this can provide valuable experience in independent and collaborative research.

Qualifications for the Field Research and Evaluation Position

Candidates interested in the field research and evaluation position should ideally have a bachelor’s or master’s degree in one of the following areas:

  • Economics
  • Public Policy
  • Development Studies
  • Statistics
  • A related quantitative or social science discipline

The strongest candidates are expected to have practical experience with field research.

Relevant experience includes:

  • Randomized controlled trials
  • Field experiments
  • Development research
  • Survey research
  • Research management
  • Field team coordination
  • Data-quality management
  • Partner coordination
  • Statistical analysis

Experience working with organizations such as J-PAL, IPA, or comparable research institutions would be an advantage.

Technical and Research Skills

Applicants should ideally have:

  • Strong applied statistics skills
  • Fluency in Stata or R
  • Familiarity with SurveyCTO or ODK
  • Understanding of survey research
  • Experience managing data collection
  • Familiarity with research ethics and IRB processes
  • Experience coordinating field teams or research partners

Fluency in Hindi or another Indian language is considered an asset, although it is not mandatory.

The ideal candidate should also be interested in understanding how AI tools perform in actual field settings and how they compare with the status quo.

Qualifications for the Tool Development and Deployment Position

Candidates applying for the technical position should ideally have a bachelor’s or master’s degree in:

  • Computer Science
  • Engineering
  • Data Science
  • A related technical discipline

Applicants should demonstrate strong programming ability and comfort working with data.

The research team is particularly interested in candidates who are curious about how technology behaves outside controlled laboratory environments.

Useful Technical Background

Coursework, research, or project experience in the following areas would be advantageous:

  • Machine learning
  • Natural language processing
  • Human-computer interaction
  • Applied statistics
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Data science
  • Software development
  • AI application development

Candidates should also be willing to spend time in the field because the position involves real-world deployment and evaluation.

The Two Positions Are Complementary

The research team has deliberately designed the two positions to complement one another.

The first fellow primarily owns the field research and evaluation side.

The second fellow primarily owns the tool development and deployment side.

This division allows the research program to combine rigorous research methodology with strong technical implementation.

However, applicants can indicate interest in either position or both positions.

Candidates who have interdisciplinary backgrounds may therefore find it useful to express interest in both roles where their experience supports both areas.

Location of the Fellowship

The fellows will be hosted at Microsoft Research in Bengaluru, India.

The position provides:

  • Desk space
  • A Microsoft Research account
  • Access to Microsoft Research resources
  • An opportunity to work alongside researchers
  • Regular travel to field locations

Fieldwork will take place in locations including:

  • Rajasthan
  • Delhi
  • Other locations in India

Applicants should therefore be prepared for a role that combines office-based research with travel and field activities.

Appointment Duration

The Research Fellow appointment is for two years.

The appointment will be made through the University of Pennsylvania Institute for the Advanced Study of India (UPIASI).

This provides fellows with the opportunity to spend an extended period working within an interdisciplinary research environment before pursuing longer-term academic or professional goals.

Compensation and Benefits

The call states that compensation will be competitive and benchmarked to Microsoft Research India Research Fellow standards.

The position also provides access to a research environment associated with both the University of Pennsylvania and Microsoft Research.

In addition to compensation, the research experience itself can be valuable for candidates preparing for future doctoral study or research-intensive careers.

Fellows will have opportunities to participate in research projects, develop technical or research-management skills, contribute to academic publications, and work with researchers and partner organizations.

Collaborating Institutions and Organizations

The research program brings together several institutions and organizations.

These include:

  • University of Pennsylvania
  • University of Pennsylvania Institute for the Advanced Study of India
  • University of Pennsylvania Center for the Advanced Study of India
  • Computational Social Listening Lab
  • Annenberg School for Communication
  • UPenn School of Nursing
  • Microsoft Research India
  • AIIMS New Delhi
  • Khushi Baby

This interdisciplinary network reflects the broad nature of the program, combining computer science, social science, health, communication, education, and field research.

Start Date

The selected candidates are expected to begin as soon as possible.

Applicants should therefore be prepared for the possibility of a relatively prompt start following selection and appointment.

Deadline for Applications

There is no fixed application deadline stated in the call.

Applications are being reviewed on a rolling basis until the positions are filled.

This means interested candidates should avoid waiting until a particular date because the recruitment process may close once suitable candidates have been selected.

Deadline: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until the positions are filled.

Early application is therefore strongly recommended.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should complete the official application form:

Apply through the official UPenn + MSR Research Fellows application form

Applicants can indicate whether they are interested in:

  • Field Research and Evaluation
  • Tool Development and Deployment
  • Both positions

Candidates should ensure that their application clearly demonstrates how their academic background, research experience, technical skills, fieldwork experience, or interdisciplinary interests relate to the program.

More information can be found HERE

For more fellowship opportunities visit the OFY Website HERE

Informal Enquiries

Candidates who have questions about the opportunity can contact one of the listed research leaders:

  • Mohit Jain
  • Gareth Nellis
  • Sharath Chandra Guntuku

For informal enquiries, applicants are instructed to use the following subject-line format:

[UPenn + MSR Research Fellow + ‘–‘ + Your Last Name]

A well-prepared enquiry should be specific and demonstrate that the applicant has reviewed the research program and understands the role they are interested in.

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity could be particularly suitable for recent graduates who are considering careers or further study in areas such as:

  • Artificial intelligence
  • Machine learning
  • Computer science
  • Data science
  • Economics
  • Development economics
  • Public policy
  • Development studies
  • Statistics
  • Public health
  • Education technology
  • Human-computer interaction
  • Natural language processing
  • Computational social science
  • Communication research
  • Media research

It may also be a strong fit for candidates who are specifically planning to pursue a Ph.D. and want to strengthen their research profile before doctoral study.

What Makes This Opportunity Different?

Several features make the fellowship particularly notable.

1. Real-world AI research

The projects are designed to move beyond theoretical AI research and examine what happens when AI tools are actually used by health workers, clinicians, students, researchers, and other users.

2. Strong interdisciplinary environment

The program combines computer science and AI with economics, public policy, health, education, communication, development research, and media studies.

3. Access to Microsoft Research

The fellows will be hosted at Microsoft Research in Bengaluru and receive access to MSR resources.

4. University of Pennsylvania affiliation

The appointment is through UPIASI, creating a connection to the University of Pennsylvania’s research ecosystem.

5. Opportunity to contribute to publications

Fellows will work as full members of the research team and contribute to research papers and other outputs.

6. Strong preparation for Ph.D. study

Because the positions are explicitly designed for recent graduates intending to pursue a Ph.D., the fellowship can provide valuable preparation for doctoral research.

7. Fieldwork experience

The positions offer exposure to real-world research environments, including field sites in India.

Application Tips

Applicants should tailor their applications to the particular position they want to pursue.

If applying for Field Research and Evaluation

Emphasize:

  • Field research experience
  • Randomized controlled trials
  • Survey research
  • Statistical analysis
  • Stata or R
  • Research management
  • Field team coordination
  • Data-quality management
  • IRB or research ethics experience
  • Work with research organizations or survey firms

If you have experience at J-PAL, IPA, or a comparable institution, make that experience prominent.

If applying for Tool Development and Deployment

Emphasize:

  • Programming skills
  • AI projects
  • Machine learning
  • NLP
  • HCI
  • Data science
  • Applied statistics
  • Software development
  • Technical research projects
  • Experience deploying technology
  • Experience working with real-world users

Applicants should not simply list programming languages or courses. Where possible, they should demonstrate what they actually built, analyzed, deployed, or researched.

If applying for both positions

Make the interdisciplinary nature of your background clear.

Explain how your skills could contribute to both:

Building and deploying AI systems

and

Evaluating those systems in real-world environments.

Important Things Applicants Should Understand

This is not presented as a conventional internship or short-term training program.

It is a two-year pre-doctoral research position intended for recent graduates planning to pursue a Ph.D.

Applicants should also understand that the work is not exclusively desk-based.

The program involves field research and deployment, including travel to locations such as Rajasthan and Delhi.

Candidates should therefore be comfortable working in environments that combine:

  • Research
  • Technology
  • Data
  • Fieldwork
  • Collaboration
  • Academic writing
  • Real-world implementation

Frequently Asked Questions

Is this a Ph.D. scholarship?

No. The opportunity is a pre-doctoral Research Fellow position, not a direct Ph.D. scholarship. It is intended for recent graduates who plan to pursue a Ph.D.

How many positions are available?

There are two positions.

One focuses on field research and evaluation, while the other focuses on tool development and deployment.

Can I apply for both positions?

Yes. Candidates may indicate interest in either or both roles.

Is there a fixed deadline?

No fixed calendar deadline is provided. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until the positions are filled.

Where is the position based?

The fellows will be hosted at Microsoft Research in Bengaluru, India.

Will the fellows travel?

Yes. The positions include regular travel to field sites, including Rajasthan, Delhi, and other locations in India.

How long is the appointment?

The appointment is for two years.

What degree is required for the field research role?

A bachelor’s or master’s degree in Economics, Public Policy, Development Studies, Statistics, or a related field is preferred.

What degree is required for the technical role?

A bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related field is preferred.

Is knowledge of Hindi required?

No. Hindi or another Indian language is an asset for the field research position but is not required.

Is programming experience required for both positions?

Strong programming skills are particularly relevant to the Tool Development and Deployment position. The Field Research and Evaluation role instead emphasizes applied statistics, research management, fieldwork, and evaluation skills.

Conclusion

The UPenn + Microsoft Research India Research Fellows Call 2026 presents an opportunity for recent graduates to participate in ambitious research examining how artificial intelligence can be designed, deployed, and evaluated in real-world settings.

The two available positions provide different but complementary pathways. The Field Research and Evaluation role is particularly suited to candidates with backgrounds in economics, public policy, development studies, statistics, and field research, while the Tool Development and Deployment role is aimed more toward candidates with backgrounds in computer science, engineering, data science, and related technical disciplines.

The research itself covers important areas including frontline healthcare, clinical communication, English-language education, entertainment media, and social norms. By combining AI development with rigorous field evaluation, the program seeks to understand not only whether AI systems can work technically, but whether they can create meaningful and sustainable improvements in people’s lives.

For recent graduates considering a future Ph.D. and interested in AI, social impact, technology, health, education, development, or interdisciplinary research, this fellowship could provide valuable hands-on research experience and exposure to an international academic and technology ecosystem.

Because applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until the positions are filled, prospective applicants should prepare their materials and submit their applications as early as possible
